props.title: MacGruber
props.initialSlug: Former special ops hero bungles mission to save world

sections.content: **MacGruber** (2010) brilliantly satirizes 1980s action movies, particularly **Rambo: First Blood** (1982) and TV's MacGyver, while creating its own absurdist identity. Will Forte's commitment to the character's simultaneously arrogant and incompetent nature elevates what could have been a one-note SNL sketch into a legitimately great comedy. Like Hot Shots! (1991) and Top Secret! (1984), MacGruber understands its source material so well that it works both as parody and as a genuine action film.

sections.content: What sets MacGruber apart from lesser parody films like **Disaster Movie** (2008) is its dedication to character-based humor rather than mere reference dropping. The film shares DNA with Black Dynamite (2009) in how it lovingly recreates the look and feel of its inspiration while adding its own twisted sensibility. The throat-ripping, celery-based humor, and sex scenes played completely straight create a unique tone that influenced later action-comedies like **21 Jump Street** (2012).

Director Jorma Taccone brings surprising technical competence to the action sequences, giving them legitimate tension even as they serve the comedy. This approach mirrors Last Action Hero (1993) in how it both celebrates and satirizes genre conventions. The villain casting of Ryan Phillippe works because, like the best action movie antagonists of the 80s, he plays it completely straight against Forte's unhinged performance. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

sections.content: MacGruber's initial box office failure but subsequent cult status follows the path of other eventually-appreciated genre parodies like **Galaxy Quest** (1999) and **They Came Together** (2014). Its influence can be seen in later works that blend extreme violence with absurdist humor, such as **The Other Guys** (2010) and **Game Over, Man!** (2018). The film's quotability and commitment to its bit have made it a touchstone for comedy writers and performers.
